content: For the management of new-onset type 2 diabetes in youth with overweight or obesity, the American Diabetes Association (ADA) recommends the following approach: 1. Initial Management: Begin with comprehensive lifestyle modifications and diabetes education for all patients. This includes dietary changes, increased physical activity, and behavioral support to promote sustainable health habits. 2. For Youth with A1C <8.5% and No Evidence of Acidosis or Ketosis: Initiate treatment with metformin. Gradually titrate the dose up to a maximum of 2,000 mg per day, as tolerated, to achieve optimal glycemic control. 3. For Youth with A1C ≥8.5% and No Evidence of Acidosis or Ketosis: Start treatment with metformin, titrating the dose up to 2,000 mg per day. Additionally, initiate long-acting insulin therapy at a starting dose of 0.5 units per kilogram of body weight per day. Adjust the insulin dose every 2 to 3 days based on blood glucose monitoring results to achieve target glucose levels. 4. For Youth Presenting with Acidosis, Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA), or Hyperosmolar Hyperglycemic State (HHS): Manage the acute condition with intravenous insulin therapy until the acidosis or hyperglycemic crisis resolves. Once stabilized, transition the patient to subcutaneous insulin therapy, following the treatment protocol for type 1 diabetes, until the results of antibody testing are available to confirm the diagnosis.
